functions.name: First-list input
functions.note: All 54 instructions represented at the Re-order callback boundary. Exact masks and native ABI replace input/context/register operations. 56914 performs the recovered availability/result contract (54B94 returns 2/3; child execution is owned by the outer dispatcher). 5696C/56988 specialize frontend state 0x0C and open the original asset-backed empty-slot message. 569A0 invokes begin-second including tint/header state; 569A8 is compiler-managed return. Modal raster/audio integration and child screens remain separate explicit gates, not credited by this owner.

functions.name: Second-list input
functions.note: All 54 instructions represented at the Re-order callback boundary. 569F0 validates child IDs and returns dispatcher code. 56A34 uses occupied/different-player validation under same-team/list-kind-2 preconditions; shared helper owners now have separate block evidence and synthetic cross-mode tests; other screens are not claimed. 56A4C performs swap and both-list rebind, 56A5C preserves the success-only continuation, 56A68 invokes finish including tint reset/header refresh/input-change barrier. State-2 skips validation/mutation/rebind. Original register/frame return is native compiler ABI. No full shared-helper or game-screen credit.

functions.name: Begin second selection
functions.note: Single 24-instruction block represented by synchronized descriptor/active/object-state values 1, second-row pulse with recovered modulation endpoints 0x80808000/0x78660000 and duration20, then refreshed selected identities/team/natural-position presentation. Asset-backed diagnostic consumes these values into real font pixels. Native retained rows replace linked text objects. Native Re-order screen consumes this state; original screenshot/timing parity remains pending.

functions.name: Finish/cancel second selection
functions.note: All 34 instructions represented: 55314 resets the active second-row tint toward neutral over8 updates, preserves the original red-channel reset quirk, restores all focus/state fields to0 and refreshes headers. 55370 represents the blocking input-change loop as a nonblocking frame barrier and latch10 (visible to the next permitted dispatch). 55380 uses compiler-managed return. Tests distinguish successful swap from cancellation, preserve scroll/previous edits, verify actual glyph reset pixels. No original framebuffer or generic input-repeat equivalence claim.

dependency_policy: Fixed inventory:875 original instructions across ten owners, now fully reviewed source-accounted at explicit native call-contract boundaries. No denominator removed. Not binary matching, full transitive coverage, original execution proof, visual fidelity or whole-feature completion. Shared Trade/Sign/Release helper branches are synthetic-tested, but those screens and their private starter-preference data provider remain unconnected. Re-order entry/selection/refresh works.
